RAJYA  SABHA
————
List of Questions for ORAL ANSWERS
to be asked at a sitting of the Rajya Sabha to be held on
Tuesday,  the March 18, 2008/Phalguna 28, 1929 (Saka)
————
(Ministries: Civil Aviation; Corporate Affairs; Culture; Finance; Heavy
Industries and Public Enterprises; Petroleum and Natural Gas;
Tourism; Water Resources)
Total number of questions — 20
81
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
Kisan Credit Cards
†*261. DR. PRABHA THAKUR: Will
the Minister of FINANCE be pleased to
state:
(a) the criteria fixed by Government for
making Kisan Credit Cards;
(b) the number of farmers provided with
Kisan Credit Cards in different States of
the country during the last three years,
State-wise; and
(c) the details of benefits of the Kisan
Credit Cards to the farmers?
Decline in ground water level
*262. SHRI C. PERUMAL:  Will the
Minister of WATER RESOURCES be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that ground water
level in various parts of the country has
declined as per the Planning Commission's
Expert Group Report;
(b) if so, the steps proposed to be taken
by Government in this regard; and
(c) the total fiscal allocation earmarked
during the last three years for the projects
regarding maintenance of ground water level,
State-wise?
Fake currency notes in ATMs
†*263. MS. SUSHILA TIRIYA:
SHRI MOTILAL VORA:
 Will the Minister of FINANCE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government is aware of
uploading of fake currency notes of
Rs. 500 into the ATMs by different banks
which not only causes financial loss to
consumers but also brings them under
suspicion;
(b) if so, the action taken, so far, by
Government against such banks; and
(c) the direction of RBI to various banks
pertaining to currency notes of Rs. 500
taken out of circulation/found fake and how
such cases are resolved by these banks?
Proposal for tourism projects in
Kerala
*264. PROF. P.J. KURIEN:  Will the
Minister of TOURISM be pleased to state:
(a) the details of projects proposals

82
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
relating to tourism received from the State
Government of Kerala for Central
assistance; and
(b) the action taken by Government in
this regard?
Interest rate on agricultural loan
†*265. SHRI RAJ MOHINDER
SINGH MAJITHA:
DR. MURLI MANOHAR
JOSHI:
 Will the Minister of FINANCE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether a demand has been made to
charge the rate of interest upto four per
cent on the agricultural loan to provide relief
to the agriculture sector;
(b) if so, when this demand first came
before Government; and
(c) the action taken so far by
Government to meet this demand?
Delay in Air India flight to
New York
*266. SHRI VIJAY J. DARDA:
SHRIMA TI SHOBHANA
BHARTIA:
 Will the Minister of CIVIL A VIATION
be pleased to state:
(a) whether an Air India flight to New
York via  London with hundreds of
passengers was delayed for more than
19 hours following a string of
misunderstandings and confusion as
reported in the media recently;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether Government has
investigated the exact cause of delay due to
which flight could not take off on time;
(d) if so, the details thereof; and
(e) the steps taken by Government to
avoid such a situation in future?
Insurance for PAN card holders
†*267. SHRI BANWARI LAL
KANCHHAL:  Will the Minister of
FINANCE be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government proposes to
provide public insurance for the Permanent
Account Number (PAN) card holders; and
(b) if so, the details thereof?
Protected monuments in Andhra
Pradesh
*268. SHRI SYED AZEEZ PASHA:
Will the Minister of CULTURE be pleased
to state:
(a) the details of protected monuments
located in Andhra Pradesh;
(b) the amount spent on the
maintenance of the said monuments during
the last three years;
(c) the revenue earned by Government
from the said monuments during the above
period; and
(d) the norms for declaring any structure
as protected monument?
Increase in administrative price of gas
*269. SHRI V. NARAYANASAMY:
Will the Minister of PETROLEUM AND
NATURAL GAS be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government
is proposing to raise the administrative
price of gas produced from fields given to
Oil and Natural Gas Corporation and Oil
India Ltd.; and

83
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
(b) if so, the price Government
proposes to fix per million cubic meter for
the gas produced by the above said
Corporations?
Relaxation in FDI limits
*270. SHRI P.R. RAJAN:  Will the
Minister of FINANCE be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government is planning to
relax Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) limits
in six more sectors, including civil aviation;
and
(b) if so, the details thereof?
Oil scenario in the country
*271. SHRI N.R. GOVINDARAJAR:
Will the Minister of PETROLEUM AND
NATURAL GAS be pleased to state:
(a) whether 90 per cent of the oil
demand of the country is met from imports;
(b) if so, the details thereof indicating
the value of oil imports during the last three
years;
(c) whether inspite of huge discovery
of oil blocks in the country, the oil import
has been increasing;
(d) if so, the details thereof with the
break up of the domestic product, import
and consumption of oil in the country
during the last three years; and
(e) the steps taken by Government to
increase the domestic production of oil and
reduce import of oil on National economy?
Credit ratio of Public Sector Banks
*272. SHRI C. RAMACHAND-
RAIAH:  Will the Minister of FINANCE
be pleased to state:
(a) whether his Ministry has directed
the Public Sector Banks to increase the
lending through their branches in the
districts in which they are the lead banks
so that the credit ratio increases from the
current level to 50 per cent in the next
twelve months;
(b) if so, the Public Sector Banks, which
have started implementing the directions
of his Ministry and in how many States
the credit ratio has been increasing
consequent to the directions; and
(c) if not, the reasons therefor and the
rationale for directing only the Bank of
Baroda to enhance the ratio  for certain
districts?
Decline in interest rate on home loans
*273. SHRIMATI JAYA BACHCHAN:
Will the Minister of FINANCE be pleased
to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that interest rate
on home loans has declined;
(b) if so, the number of occasions on
which it has declined during the last one
year;
(c) whether it is also a fact that the
benefit of declined rate of interest is not
being passed on to the existing borrowers;
and
(d) if so, what are the reasons for
differential rate of interest for existing as
well as new borrowers?
Exploration work for oil and gas in
Rajasthan
†*274. SHRI LALIT KISHORE
CHATURVEDI:
DR. GYAN PRAKASH
PILANIA:
Will the Minister of PETROLEUM
AND NATURAL GAS be pleased to
state:

84
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
(a) the places in Rajasthan where the
work for oil and natural gas exploration is
going on;
(b) the details of the companies
entrusted with this work;
(c) the number of proposals for
exploration work and the level at which
they are lying pending; and
(d) the results of exploration work made
till date?
Tourist spots in the North-Eastern
Region
*275. SHRI MATILAL SARKAR: Will
the Minister of TOURISM be pleased to
state:
(a) the number of tourist spots coming
under Central assistance, State-wise;
(b) how many of them are in the North-
Eastern Region; and
(c) the details of these tourist spots in
the North-Eastern Region?
Agreement in hydrocarbons field with
USA
*276. SHRI MATI VIPLOVE
THAKUR: Will the Minister of
PETROLEUM AND NA TURAL GAS be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that India has
signed an agreement with the United States
of America (USA) for cooperation in the
fields of hydrocarbons;
(b) if so, the details in this regard
including the objectives India has to meet
and the benefits it is likely to receive under
the agreement;
(c) whether it is also a fact that
obligations on the country outweigh the
benefits likely to be received; and
(d) if so, the reasons therefor?
Problems faced by RRBs
†*277. SHRI MANGANI LAL
MANDAL: Will the Minister of
FINANCE  be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that despite
reconstitution of all the Regional Rural
Banks (RRBs) in the country, these banks
are not only running under losses but have
also failed to achieve their targets;
(b) whether it is also a fact that given
the dominance of sponsoring banks, RRBs
are facing difficulty in their independent
development and working; and
(c) if so, the details thereof, State-wise
and bank-wise?
Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel Memorial
*278. SHRI KANJIBHAI PA TEL:
SHRI JAYANTILAL BAROT:
Will the Minister of CULTURE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government is considering
to give corpus fund for development and
maintenance of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel
Memorial at Karamsad;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) if not, the reasons therefor?
Marine aquarium at Puri in Orissa
*279. MS. PRAMILA BOHIDAR:
SHRI B.J. PANDA:
Will the Minister of TOURISM be
pleased to state:
(a) whether the State Government of
Orissa proposes to set up a state-of-the-
art marine aquarium at Puri to boost tourism
in this region;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and

85
(c) what is the action plan of the Central
Government to help the State to
successfully execute this project?
Tourism infrastructure for World
Heritage Sites in the country
*280. SHRIMA TI SUPRIYA SULE:
Will the Minister of TOURISM be pleased
to state:
(a) whether her Ministry has identified
creation of tourism infrastucture at World
Heritage Sites as a priority and efforts are
being made to have better coordination with
N
EW DELHI; V . K. AGNIHOTRI,
The 12th March, 2008 Secretary-General.
Phalguna 22, 1929 (Saka)
the Ministries of Civil Aviation, Railways,
Surface Transport and Urban Development
and respective State Governments to
execute these projects expeditiously;
(b) whether her Ministry has
discussed the issue with Prime Minister
on the areas where better coordination
was required among various Central
Ministries for promotion of tourism and
betterment of related infrastructure in the
country; and
(c) what are the concrete steps and
measures taken to facelift the World
Heritage Sites in the country?

I N D E X
(Ministry-wise)
Civil Aviation : 266,
Corporate Affairs :—
Culture : 268, 278,
Finance : 261, 263, 265, 267, 270, 272, 273, 277,
Heavy Industries and Public
Enterprises :—
Petroleum and Natural Gas : 269, 271, 274, 276,
Tourism : 264, 275, 279, 280,
Water Resources : 262.
86
